title: A simple weekly content routine
desc: Monday: pick one topic and write three hooks. Tuesday: draft the script and shot list. Wednesday: record or generate the clips. Thursday: edit, add…
text: Monday: pick one topic and write three hooks. Tuesday: draft the script and shot list. Wednesday: record or generate the clips. Thursday: edit, add captions, export two versions. Friday: post and reply to comments in the first hour. Saturday: check which hook performed best and write it down. Sunday: rest, then repeat with the best hook as your starting point. Keep a simple note with the date, hook, result and one lesson for each post so your next week gets easier.

title: Find your first three clients with content
desc: Pick one problem you can solve, such as product photos for small shops or captions for busy owners. Day 1 to 3: make three before-and-after examples.…
text: Pick one problem you can solve, such as product photos for small shops or captions for busy owners. Day 1 to 3: make three before-and-after examples. Day 4 to 7: post one example a day and say who it's for. Day 8 to 10: message ten people you already know who need it, and offer one small paid job. Day 11 to 14: ask for feedback and a short quote, then post the result. Be honest about what you offer, show real work only, and never promise results you can't control.

title: Turn one idea into five posts
desc: 1) Write your idea as one clear sentence. 2) Make a 30-second video that explains it. 3) Cut the strongest 10 seconds as a teaser. 4) Turn the main…
text: 1) Write your idea as one clear sentence. 2) Make a 30-second video that explains it. 3) Cut the strongest 10 seconds as a teaser. 4) Turn the main points into a 5-slide carousel. 5) Post the single best line as a text or quote card. 6) Turn viewers' questions into your next idea. One idea can feed a whole week when you reshape it for each format.

title: Google Flow: free daily credits
desc: Try AI video with a free daily credit allowance.
text: Google Flow gives free users a daily credit allowance (reported at 50 credits a day, with no rollover). Enough for a few short clips. Check the app for what you have today.

title: ChatGPT free plan
desc: Ideas, scripts and a few images a day.
text: The free plan covers brainstorming, scripts and captions, plus a small daily image allowance. See Settings, then Usage, to check your limits.

title: Gemini: free image creation
desc: Create images in the Gemini app at no cost.
text: Free Gemini users can make roughly 20 images a day with Nano Banana 2. Limits change, so check the app.

title: CapCut: free editor
desc: A free editor with captions and templates.
text: The free plan covers core editing. Some effects and AI features are paid or capped, so check what's included before you rely on one.

title: Research tools: NotebookLM and Perplexity
desc: Two free tools for fact-checking and research.
text: NotebookLM answers questions about only the sources you upload. Perplexity gives answers with sources you can open. Use both to check your script before you publish.

title: Sora has shut down
desc: OpenAI closed Sora in 2026. Here's what to use instead.
text: OpenAI's Sora web app closed on April 26, 2026 and its API on September 24, 2026. Main alternatives now: Google Veo 3.1 (via Flow), Kling, Runway and Seedance.
